title: Contract redline routing and legal risk escalation for enterprise offers
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a prescriptive playbook that defines how commercial contract redlines (MSA/DPA, liability, indemnity, data clauses) are triaged, routed, and escalated for enterprise prospects. This ticket covers the routing matrix, risk categories, SLA targets for Legal review, and integration points with pricing/packaging experiments and security questionnaire responses.

Background:
Sales and Solutions Engineering are increasingly seeing bespoke redlines as part of high-value deals. Current handling is ad-hoc: CC to general counsel, long turnarounds, and inconsistent commercial outcomes. This causes friction in closing enterprise deals and prevents predictable packaging/pricing for Dedicated/Private offerings.

Goals:
- Reduce average legal review turnaround for redlines to <= 5 business days for standard risk buckets.
- Create clear routing rules so sales can self-serve with minimal legal intervention for low-risk redlines.
- Define a risk escalation matrix tied to specific contract clauses (liability caps, indemnity carve-outs, data residency, security questionnaire failures).
- Ensure pricing/packaging experiments incorporate contract flexibility boundaries so product and sales incentives align with legal risk.
- Produce a standard DPA template and a redline annotation guide for SEs.

Scope (what this ticket covers):
- Routing playbook for MSA/DPA/DPA+SLA redlines.
- Risk categories and decision table mapping clauses to reviewers and approval authorities.
- SLAs for Legal and TPM responses.
- Integration notes for Sales CRM to auto-tag risk buckets and attach security questionnaires.
- Example responses to common security questionnaire items for cloud/private deployments.

Out of scope:
- Full DPA rewrite (we will reference existing legal templates).
- Negotiation playbook for downstream partner legal teams (separate enablement).

Proposed workflow (high level):
1) Sales/SE receives redline from customer and submits to Zendesk/Contract intake form that includes: contract type, key redlined clauses, customer size, requested financial terms, and security questionnaire status.
2) Intake system auto-classifies redline into risk bucket (Low / Medium / High) using rule engine based on clause keywords and deal attributes.
3) Low risk -> SE-led response using annotated DPA and pre-approved fallback language (no Legal review required unless flagged).
4) Medium risk -> Product counsel (in-house) review within 3 business days; may consult Head of Revenue Ops for pricing tradeoffs.
5) High risk -> Escalate to General Counsel + CRO review with target 5 business day SLA and mandatory risk memo.
6) For any redline that impacts pricing/packaging (e.g., capacity guarantees, exclusivity, or special SLAs), loop in PM owner for pricing experiment impact assessment before sign-off.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Sales/SE: ensure intake form is complete, pre-validate against playbook.
- Revenue Ops: configure intake automation and maintain clause-to-bucket rules.
- Legal/Product Counsel: review Medium/High redlines, maintain annotated templates, and capture precedent.
- PM (this ticket owner): maintain mapping between contract flexibility and pricing experiment guardrails.
- Engineering (Infra/Private): advise on feasibility for technical asks in DPAs/SLAs (e.g., data residency, on-prem upgrades).

Risk categories and escalation matrix (examples):
- Low: Minor language clarifications, non-substantive formatting, standard indemnity language present. Reviewer: SE with template.
- Medium: Liability cap adjustments within 2x baseline, standard indemnity substitutions, non-production data requests. Reviewer: Product Counsel.
- High: Unlimited liability, punitive damages, broad indemnity, new data residency commitments, SLA financial credits > 1% ARR. Reviewer: GC + CRO.

SLA targets:
- Intake acknowledgment: within 24 hours.
- Low bucket turnaround: 2 business days.
- Medium bucket turnaround: 3 business days.
- High bucket turnaround: 5 business days for preliminary decision; final memo within 10 business days.

Pricing/packaging experiment integration notes:
- Any redline that requests change to capacity guarantees, reserved capacity commitments, or billing cadence must spawn a short pricing impact assessment (template) capturing expected ARR delta, unit economics impact, and recommended SKU adjustments.
- Create a gating rule: pricing concessions > 15% or custom billing terms require VP-Sales approval and trigger the High risk flow.
- Maintain a weekly ledger of redline-driven concessions to inform A/B pricing experiments and make packaging adjustments in next product cycle.

Security questionnaire touchpoints:
- Intake must attach latest vendor questionnaire (e.g., SIG, CAIQ) and a summary of any failed controls.
- Failed critical controls add +1 risk bucket.
- Create standard language for DPA responses to the top 10 repeated security questions for Private/VPC deployments.

Acceptance criteria (must be true for this ticket to be Done):
- A documented playbook (Confluence link) with routing matrix and example clause mappings.
- Intake form prototype built in Zendesk with auto-classification rules stubbed.
- Three annotated template artifacts: DPA baseline, errata for low-risk edits, and medium-risk counsel notes.
- SLA metrics dashboard (New Relic/Grafana or Ops Console) that surfaces intake count and turnaround times.
- Playbook reviewed and approved by GC and Head of Revenue Ops.

QA and rollout plan:
- Pilot with two AE pods for 4 weeks; collect metrics and refine rules.
- Train SEs with one 60-minute workshop and checkbox-based intake checklist.
- Iterate the rule engine based on false positives/negatives logged during pilot.

Open questions (requires Legal/Product decisions):
- What is the default liability cap for Dedicated vs. Private customers? (Legal to propose ranges.)
- Do we allow customer-supplied DPA templates for customers > $10M ARR?
- How many pricing concessions can Sales apply without VP sign-off? (Recommend 15% cap.)

Next steps:
- 2025-02-20: Run alignment workshop with Legal, Revenue Ops, and Head of PM. (Done)
- 2025-02-25: Draft intake form and rule set (in-progress).
- 2025-03-07: Deliver annotated DPA and medium-risk guidance for legal review.
- 2025-03-15: Begin pilot with AE pods.

Related links: see related_links field for documents and templates.

implementation_notes: Keep an audit trail of all redline decisions and store precedent snippets in a searchable repo. Build a small precedence registry (CSV initially) mapping clause language to final disposition and deal terms. Legal to capture rationale for each high-risk deviation.
owner_notes: This ticket ties directly to pricing experiments: PMs must ensure any approved concession feeds the packaging ledger. If Legal asks for changes that materially increase unit cost, require the PM to propose compensating guardrails.
qa_plan: Pilot with two AE pods, collect 4 key metrics (turnaround, escalations, deal slippage, concession $ impact). Weekly retro to refine rules.
